# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫱 👌 ☝ 🤟 ✌ 👎 🫲 🤟 👎 ✌ ☝ 👌 🫲 ✌ 🤟 ☝ 👌 👎 🫲 👎 👌 ☝ 🤟 ✌ 🫲 ☝ 🤟 ✌ 👌 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I can see the bomb’s complete visible state: display 9, green indicator, and five wires in order: white, green, red, yellow, purple. I cannot verify the meaning of the long gesture sequence without an agreed code. I’m sending the bomb facts to both teammates; Mute should apply the manual and tell Blind the required action in speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 9. Light is green. Wires in order: 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Please read the manual and speak the exact required action to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb visible facts: display 9; green light; wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Wait for Mute's manual-derived instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Mute sent 🤟, but no gesture code was established, so I cannot safely interpret it as an instruction. The manual-derived answer still needs to reach Blind through Mute’s speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely interpret 🤟 without an agreed code. Please speak the exact manual instruction for display 9, green light, and wires white-green-red-yellow-purple directly to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe action has been established yet. Please rely on Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

Mute has sent three identical upward-pointing gestures. Since Blind cannot see gestures, I should relay their literal form by speech rather than guess their meaning. I still do not know the agreed code or the manual’s required action, so Blind must not act on this alone.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest signal is: up-pointing index gesture, up-pointing index gesture, up-pointing index gesture. This is a literal relay, not a decoded action.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind cannot see your gestures. Please use the agreed gesture code consistently, and I will relay each symbol by name to Blind; do not rely on Blind seeing the gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

The repeated three 👆 gestures still have no established meaning. Since Mute can read the manual and speak, the safe channel to Blind is Mute’s voice; Mute must state the exact operation, including which wire or control and any required sequence. I will not invent a decoding.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind now. Include the required wire/control and every step; gestures cannot reach Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The repeated three up-pointing gestures are not a decoded instruction. Do not act until Mute speaks the exact manual procedure.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆]

The repeated signal is still the only information from Mute, and no action code has been agreed. I will establish a minimal code rather than guess: a run of 👆 means the wire number, and ✊ will mean cut. Thus the current three 👆 can identify wire 3, but do not yet establish that it should be cut. Mute should confirm the operation using the code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code: a run of 👆 gives the wire number; then send ✊ for cut, 👍 for hold, 👎 for do not cut. Send the wire-number run, then the operation symbol. Your current 👆 👆 👆 identifies wire 3, but operation is still unknown.")
speak(to="blind", text="I am establishing a code with Mute: repeated up-pointing gestures give the wire number, and a following symbol will specify the operation. The current three gestures identify wire 3 only; do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 ✊]

Mute has now sent the established code for wire 3 followed by the cut command: 👆 👆 👆 ✊. I will relay that as “cut the third wire,” which is the red wire. Blind should perform only that operation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction: cut wire 3, the red wire. Perform only that operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 ✊]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous instruction was accepted: cutting wire 3 was correct. The bomb has changed to display 4 with a yellow light; wire 3 is now cut, and the other wires remain white, green, yellow, purple. Mute’s repeated signal is not yet a complete new instruction unless its final ✊ is again the cut command, so I will ask Mute to provide the next wire number and operation using the established code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 4, light yellow; wire 3 is cut, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple remain. Please send the next required wire number followed by the operation using our code: repeated 👆 for wire number, then ✊ cut, 👍 hold, or 👎 do not cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="The previous cut was correct. New state: display 4, yellow light; wire 3 is cut; wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple remain. Await Mute's next coded instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 8

DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✊]

Mute’s coded instruction is five 👆 gestures followed by ✊: cut wire 5. The current visible state has wire 5 purple, so Blind should cut the purple wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction: cut wire 5, the purple wire. Perform only that operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 9

DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✊]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The cut of wire 5 was accepted and correct. The bomb has changed to display 3 with a green light; wires 3 and 5 are cut, while wires 1 white, 2 green, and 4 yellow remain. The gesture currently visible repeats the already-used instruction for wire 5, so I will not treat it as a new command.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 was correct. New state: display 3, green light; wires 3 and 5 cut; wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow remain. Please send the next wire number and operation, not the previous wire-5 instruction.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 5 was correct. New state: display 3, green light; wires 3 and 5 are cut; wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow remain. The repeated signal is the old wire-5 instruction; await Mute's new instruction.")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✊]
